definition: IBM ViaVoice was a range of language-specific continuous speech recognition software products offered by IBM.
details: The current version is designed primarily for use in embedded devices. The latest stable version of IBM Via Voice was 9.0 and was able to transfer text directly into Microsoft Word. The most important process for the correct use of this software is the so-called 'quick training', and 'enrollment': it consists of reading many specific words and sentences in order to make the software adapt itself to the specific users' sound and intonation features. It lasts for one hour or more and can be divided in many parts. Users are able to improve decoding accuracy, by reading prepared texts of a few hundred sentences. The recorded data was used to tune the acoustic model to that specific user. In addition, user specific text files could be parsed to tune the language model. Correction of mis-recognised words was also used to improve subsequent decode accuracy.

explainer.lead: IBM ViaVoice was a range of language-specific continuous speech recognition software products. It brought speaker-adapted dictation to desktop and embedded use.

tiers.eli5: It's software that learns how you talk by having you read aloud, then types what you say.
tiers.practitioner: Getting good results depends on 'quick training' and 'enrollment', where the user reads many specific words and sentences for an hour or more so the software adapts to their sound and intonation. Skipping it hurts accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: The latest stable version was 9.0 and could transfer text directly into Microsoft Word; the current version is designed primarily for embedded devices.

explainer.example: A user reads the enrollment sentences for an hour, after which dictated text goes straight into Microsoft Word.
